teams.heading: Mark Nawaqanitawase weighing switch of allegiance from Wallabies to Fiji
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase has not yet confirmed his international allegiance, and reports now have his Wallabies future in doubt as he considers a switch to Fiji. Sir Steve Hansen said in October that "Mark Nawaqanitawase would be better off playing for Fiji", while Wallabies boss Les Kiss has stayed coy about what was discussed with the player. The matter stays open until Nawaqanitawase confirms his allegiance or plays a Test for either side.

teams.heading: Alex Mitchell ruled out of England's November Nations Championship with hamstring injury
teams.body: The hamstring injury Mitchell suffered in Northampton's win over Gloucester last weekend also rules him out of the finals weekend later this month. Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies. Fin Smith, the flyhalf, has a calf problem and took part in limited training on Tuesday; Borthwick has given him until Wednesday to prove he can play, with George Ford and Marcus Smith on standby.

lead.why: A fresh injury blow to England's own squad, with concrete facts on who is out and who is in line to replace him.

teams.heading: Clermont add All Blacks prop Ofa Tu'ungafasi as three-month front-row cover
teams.body: The Top 14 club announced on Tuesday that the 34-year-old has joined on a short-term deal. Their front row is already stretched: Cristian Ojovan and Sacha Lotrian are injured, and scrum anchor Regis Montagne is away with France this month. Tu'ungafasi can play tighthead or loosehead, and he played the last of his 68 Tests in November 2024 and featured for the Blues in this year's Super Rugby. Clermont, ninth in the Top 14, head to leaders Toulouse on Saturday.

lead.why: A fresh, concrete club signing that ties a French front-row shortage to Régis Montagne's international call-up, and it is not a repeat of the Le Garrec and Graou story.

teams.heading: Ulster wing Rob Baloucoune wants first try of season against Argentina
teams.body: Baloucoune hasn't scored a try yet this season, and the Ulster wing wants that to change when Argentina visit Aviva Stadium. He has played little so far, and this week's game will be his fourth of the campaign, but he is the kind of player who wants his name on the scoresheet. "Every time I'm on the pitch, I want to score," he says. The 29-year-old scored 12 tries in 13 appearances for Ulster, Ireland and Ireland A last season.

lead.why: A fresh, quotable Ireland player story with a clear angle on the Argentina game, ahead of the Nations Championship opener.

teams.heading: Quesada names 33-man squad as 15 Italy players miss Springboks Test
teams.body: Italy have confirmed 15 key men are unavailable through injury for the Turin Test against South Africa, including captain Michele Lamaro and Tommaso Menoncello, with Ignacio Brex and Sebastian Negri also out. Tighthead Marco Riccioni is unavailable for family reasons. Quesada has still named a 33-man squad, recalling Ange Capuozzo for the first time since the Six Nations and calling up five uncapped players, including former Argentina international Domingo Miotti. Quesada says he has "complete confidence in the players available."

teams.heading: Justin Marshall warns Scotland must not go insular against All Blacks
teams.body: Justin Marshall, the former All Blacks scrum-half, tells Planet Rugby that Scotland must keep attacking against New Zealand this weekend. Last year Scotland came back from 17-0 down to 17-all before Damian McKenzie's cameo rescued the visitors. "They went insular, started kicking the ball away," Marshall said, and Kieran Read adds that Scotland have too often lost the big games. Planet Rugby also points to wins over England, France and Argentina this year as proof of what Scotland can do.

lead.why: It is the freshest item with concrete match facts, and its warning to Scotland about playing insular rugby is aimed at the home side's mindset.

teams.heading: Peter Murchie demands major improvement from Wales defence before Japan clash
teams.body: Wales resume their Nations Championship campaign against Japan on Saturday with the defence under the spotlight. Murchie, in his second campaign on Steve Tandy's staff, was unhappy with the summer: Wales missed more than 100 tackles and conceded 15 tries across three games, beating Fiji but losing to Argentina and South Africa. "We're here to win Test matches, we're not here to take part and we've spoken about that as a group," he said. Wales have won only three of their 12 Tests under Tandy.

lead.why: A new, on-the-record intervention from Wales's defence coach, with concrete summer figures, ahead of this Saturday's match against Japan.

teams.heading: Cheika says Contepomi came into coaching 'raw' before Pumas job
teams.body: Michael Cheika, who coached Felipe Contepomi at Leinster two decades ago, says his former fly-half came into coaching raw and had to learn the trade properly. Contepomi later spent four seasons as Leinster's attack coach before Cheika brought him into the Pumas set-up. Joe Schmidt, who coached Australia against Argentina in 2024 and 2025, calls him a 'pretty good friend', and the pair each won two of those four Rugby Championship meetings.

teams.heading: Les Kiss adds Kurtley Beale to Wallabies spring tour squad
teams.body: Hunter Paisami's personal withdrawal opened the door for Kurtley Beale, 37, who returns to the Wallabies' spring tour after five years away from Test rugby. Beale has 95 caps and comes in after back-to-back Bledisloe Cup defeats to New Zealand. Kiss insists the recall is about depth at flyhalf, where he still has to settle on a World Cup starter. "He’s in there to perform." He will reassess the position after the next Super Rugby Pacific season.

lead.why: Item #1 is about Joe Schmidt's Ulster role, not Australia (it fails the Australia test), so the Beale recall, the freshest Australia selection item in the pack, leads.

teams.heading: Wales sell out Principality lower tier for Japan test as demand grows
teams.body: The WRU has added Under 18s tickets in the middle and upper tiers, with thousands of supporters expected in Cardiff for Japan's visit. Cheaper entry remains available: £16 for under-18s accompanying an adult, £22 for students and adults from £31. Fan Zone Cymru opens at Cardiff Arms Park with free entry, and a junior tag festival runs alongside it for players from 25 community clubs.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item on the shortlist, and the other candidates are either already-reported Willemse coverage or background pieces.

teams.heading: All Blacks head of security Logan Cadwallader dies suddenly in Edinburgh
teams.body: NZ Rugby has confirmed that the team's security chief of the past decade died after a medical event at its Edinburgh hotel. Coach Dave Rennie said: "We are all devastated." Cadwallader had served in the New Zealand Army and Special Air Service Regiment, with deployments to Bosnia, East Timor, Afghanistan and the Solomon Islands. Assistant coach Jason Ryan called him the squad's quiet hero as the team prepares for Saturday's Test against Scotland at Murrayfield.

lead.why: The most widely corroborated new item, and it concerns the All Blacks' own management group ahead of the Scotland Test.

teams.heading: Erasmus says Boks may need to win out to reach Nations final
teams.body: Erasmus has spelled out the arithmetic behind the Springboks' Nations Championship hopes. SuperSport Rugby's clip has him saying the side may need to win every remaining match and edge the All Blacks on points difference to make the final. That lands on a side that has won all three of its matches so far in the inaugural competition, with Saturday's match against Italy the first step. He also explains what would prompt the Springboks to "experiment like hell" in Europe.

lead.why: A new coach's-eye item with a concrete condition for reaching the final, unlike the uncapped-players story already run on Tuesday.
